title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatics for 'analysis situs' (tame or stratified topology) in terms of 'atlases' A=(𝔉,≤,≪). Here 𝔉 is a set of 'figures', each figure is identified with the poset of its closed strata, ≤ is the sub-figure order and ≪ is refinement. On this page he isolates two combinatorial regularity conditions on the stratum posets.

(1) Polyideal posets. A poset I is 'polyidéal' if any two elements with a common lower bound have an infimum. Equivalently, for x,y∈I with I_{≤x}∩I_{≤y}≠∅, that intersection has a greatest element. If the relevant subsets are inductive (automatic in the finite case), this is equivalent to the nonempty set I_{≤x}∩I_{≤y} being filtered (directed). That is the 4-variable condition: for all x,y,x',y' with x',y' ≤ x,y there exists z with x',y' ≤ z ≤ x,y.
- Converting directed to greatest element uses Zorn plus directedness: a maximal element of a directed set is its greatest element.
- The 4-variable form is invariant under reversing the order and swapping (x,y)↔(x',y'), so it is self-dual. Under dual inductivity hypotheses it therefore also says that two elements with a common upper bound have a supremum.
- Lemma: if all intervals [x',x] are inductive (e.g. finite), then I polyideal ⇔ I^op polyideal.

(2) Polyideal figures and atlases. A figure F is polyideal if its poset of strata is: two non-disjoint closed strata meet in a closed stratum. An atlas is polyideal if all its figures are. This is phrased as a condition on the poset M of all strata:
- At pol 1: for X,Y∈M that are compatible (sub-figures of a common figure) and non-disjoint (i.e. {X,Y} has a lower bound in M), Inf^{M,≤}(X,Y) exists.

(3) Simplicial posets. A combinatorial simplex is a poset isomorphic to P*(J), the nonempty subsets of a finite set J. A poset I is 'simplicial' if every lower set I_{≤x} is a combinatorial simplex. A figure is simplicial if its stratum poset is.
- He then sketches a characterization: S is a combinatorial simplex iff S is finite, polyideal, has a greatest element, and every non-minimal element has at least two predecessors.
- The proof sketch (continued on p.14) is by induction on card S. Every element is the sup of the minimal elements below it, and with J the set of minimal elements one gets S≃P*(J).

Purpose: to formulate the 'axiomes spéciaux' distinguishing polyhedral atlases (strata meet in strata, as for polyhedral/regular-cell stratifications) from simplicial ones. This prepares the compatibility axiom Ax C on p.14.
errors:
The sketched characterization of combinatorial simplices is false as stated (as far as the text is legible). Take the face poset of a square (4 vertices, 4 edges, one top cell).
- It is finite, has a greatest element, and is polyideal: adjacent edges meet in a vertex, opposite edges are not minorized, edge∧top = edge.
- Every non-minimal element has at least two immediate predecessors.
- Yet it is not ≅P*(J): the induction step fails because a proper subset of the minimal elements (two opposite vertices) has sup equal to the top.
A correct criterion needs more, e.g. that the map x ↦ {minimal elements below x} is surjective onto P*(J), or that lower intervals are Boolean (each element of rank k covers exactly k+1 elements). The weaker Axiom 1 on p.14 (∂X empty or with ≥2 maximal elements) is clearly not meant to characterize simplices.
Slip: 'deux éléments majorés de I ont un plus grand élément' should read 'have a supremum' (least common upper bound), the dual of the inf statement.

The equivalence 'greatest element ⇔ filtered' needs inductivity of I_{≤x}∩I_{≤y} itself (or of the intervals), not just of I. Grothendieck flags this vaguely with '(strict)' and '(vrai si fini)', so the hypothesis is stated loosely but the idea is right.

ideas.what: Polyideal poset: any two elements with a common lower bound have a meet; equivalent finitary self-dual 4-point filteredness condition; lemma that I polyideal ⇔ I^op polyideal under finiteness of intervals.
ideas.modern_name: Poset with meets of bounded-below pairs (locally a meet-semilattice); 'intersection property' of polyhedral/regular cell complexes; finite case = S∪{0̂} a lattice when S has a top
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in lattice theory / combinatorial topology (e.g. polytopal complexes, Björner's regular CW complexes)

ideas.what: Polyideal atlas: axiom At pol 1 requiring that non-disjoint compatible strata have an infimum stratum (two closed strata meet in a closed stratum).
ideas.modern_name: Intersection condition for polyhedral complexes / 'regular' stratifications in tame topology
ideas.where_published: Spirit of 'tame topology' announced in Esquisse d'un programme, but this axiom is not published there

ideas.what: Simplicial ordered set: every lower set I_{≤x} is isomorphic to P*(J), J finite; simplicial figures/stratifications. Combined with polyideal, this gives exactly face posets of simplicial complexes.
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial poset (Boolean cell complex); together with the meet condition, the face poset of an abstract simplicial complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Garsia (1980, 'Boolean cell complexes'), Björner (1984), Stanley (1991, simplicial posets)

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently introduces 'simplicial ordered sets' (all lower intervals Boolean, i.e. ≅P*(J)), which are exactly the simplicial posets of Garsia/Björner/Stanley. He separates them from the 'polyideal' meet condition, and their conjunction gives simplicial complexes. He embeds this in an axiomatics of stratified 'atlases' with a refinement relation ≪. This links poset-theoretic combinatorial topology to his tame-topology program, a link not made in the literature.
missed.quote: Un ens. ordonné I est dit simplicial, s'il ... pour tout x∈I, S=I_{≤x} est un ... simplexe combinatoire, i.e. isomorphe à ... 𝔓*(J)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck's tame topology was meant to be organized combinatorially by stratum posets with regularity axioms. This is close to modern exit-path / poset-stratified-space approaches (Lurie's stratified spaces, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine order-theoretic definitions: meet condition, self-duality lemma, simplicial posets. They are known in combinatorics (simplicial posets, ca. 1980–91) and here serve as scaffolding for the unpublished atlas axiomatics. The only interest is historical/contextual, plus a flawed characterization of combinatorial simplices.
transcription_corrections: In At pol 1 the relation written 'X \not\geq_M Y' is most likely the compatibility symbol 'X ≍_M Y' (sub-figures of a common figure), as used on p.14 ('X ≍ Y', 'F ≍ G'), not '≱'.
The text reads 'Inf^{M,≤}(X,Y) existe' with the parenthetical '{X,Y} minoré dans M)' clarifying 'non disjoints'.
Line 'Quand I est un ens. inductif (strict) (vrai si fini), il revient au même de dire que ... I_{≤x}∩I_{≤y} est filtrant'. The word 'filtrant' is legible.

Top-left margin note reads roughly: 'cela signifie aussi que [dans une figure] toute intersection de deux strates fermées non disjointes est une strate fermée' (a gloss on the polyideal condition for figures).
Bottom-left margin: 'Définition des atlas polyidéaux, ou condition de l'At[las] intersection'.
